title: POC Weekly Sync - Model Selection & Pinning
next_steps: Redwood to share updated benchmark sheet with per-model latency/cost columns
Customer to run internal evals on the pinned model using sample prompts by next Friday
Schedule canary deploy for fallback flow next week with SRE team
action_items: Carlos Ruiz: update benchmark spreadsheet with 8k context results and quantization notes by 2027-01-22
Lina Zhou: run eval harness against 50 production prompts and return accuracy/scorecard by 2027-01-28
Maya Patel: send contract addendum and security pack (SOC2 + SAML docs) by 2027-01-21
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review model selection and pinning strategy. Discussed benchmark results, rollback/fallback options, and security requirements. Agreed to pin v3-small for low-latency routes and keep v2-quant as fallback; run canary with SRE next week.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, we know lots on the agenda for today, quick check on time can we go 45 minutes?
[00:10] Marcus (Acme): Yep that's fine, we have about half our team online.
[01:05] Carlos (Redwood SE): Cool, i'll start with the benchmark snapshot we ran this morning, i included 2-second median numbers and p95s, bear in mind these are running on the dedicated cluster with 8k context for the v3-small tests.
[02:30] Lina (Acme): quick question, the sheet says q4 quantized results for v2-quant are much cheaper but p95 is higher, do you have the exact numbers?
[02:45] Carlos: yeah, so v3-small median is ~220ms per token, p95 ~480ms; v2-quant median ~140ms but p95 spikes to ~1.2s on long sequences. cost per 1k tokens: v3-small is about $0.012, v2-quant about $0.006. those are ballpark.
[04:00] Jared (Acme): okay that matches what we saw in dev. latency matters for our checkout chat flow so we're worried about p95.
[04:20] Maya: sounds like a classic latency vs cost decision, for checkout we recommend pinning to the lower-latency model and using the quantized variant as a fallback for non-time-sensitive routes.
[05:10] Tom (SRE): can you explain fallback mechanics? what happens if the pinned model is saturated?
[05:30] Carlos: yes, so Redwood routing supports policy-based fallback: if the primary hits concurrency threshold or crosses error rate/rate limit, it routes to a compatible model variant. we've implemented automatic prefix cache reuse where possible, but note some models' KV cache shapes are incompatible so cold starts can still happen.
[06:40] Priya (Security): a couple security items: we need confirmation on where logs live, retention policy, and KMS/HSM usage for keys. also SSO/SAML requirements - we can't use just local accounts.
[07:05] Maya: understood, i'll attach the SOC2 pack and our SAML SSO guide after. Redwood supports customer-managed keys via KMS for Private and Dedicated deployments.
[08:15] Marcus: good. back to pinning: what do you mean by "compatible model variant"? is v2-quant considered compatible with v3-small?
[08:30] Carlos: compatible in terms of API and response format, yes, but quality differs, and prompts may need tuning; we also support automated fallback that rewrites model params to preserve widest compatibility. think of it as graceful degradation.
[09:50] Lina: any feature for canary/rollbacks? we want to test for hallucination/regression on a subset of traffic.
[10:05] Carlos: absolutely, our rollout supports canary by percentage; you can pin a route to a model and do 10% canary then roll to 100% or rollback. rollbacks are immediate if error thresholds hit. we've seen in trials that latent regressions happen with new quant profiles, so we recommend an A/B with eval harness for the first week.
[11:35] Jared: do you keep old weights for a rollback or do you deploy a new container? what's the recovery time?
[11:55] Carlos: good question — we keep the pinned version in the model catalog and the runtime can warm it. recovery depends on cache warmup but in our Dedicated clusters we've seen 95th percentile failover in under a minute if the model is warm, up to a few minutes cold.
[13:05] Tom: that cold start is a concern. can we pre-warm the fallback?
[13:20] Carlos: yes, pre-warm hooks exist; you can schedule warm-up or keep a minimal replica for fallback. that's part of the config we'll suggest in the playbook.
[14:10] Maya: okay next, i want to propose a pinning strategy for Acme: pin route /checkout to v3-small:v3.1 (stable) for latency, set fallback to v2-quant:v2.4, and a canary for v3-medium in 10% traffic after two days of evals. Thoughts?
[15:00] Marcus: that seems reasonable, as long as fallback doesn't degrade the user experience too badly. we'll accept a small degradation during high load but not during regular checkout.
[16:00] Lina: for evaluation we'll need a quality scorecard, what metrics do you advise?
[16:20] Carlos: typical: exact match for structured responses, BLEU/perplexity for free text is noisy so we recommend a rubric-based eval plus business metrics like conversion delta and safety/hallucination flags. we'll share our eval harness and sample prompts.
[17:45] Priya: on compliance, we need audit logs for model access per token and role-based access control to limit who can pin models. do you provide role-level permissions?
[18:05] Maya: yes RBAC is supported; you can restrict pin/rollout to admin groups. audit logs are in the Console and we can set retention to meet your policy; longer retention is an add-on.
[19:10] Marcus: any known incompatibilities for our planned VPC Dedicated setup? we run in GCP with private peering.
[19:30] Carlos: we've onboarded several GCP VPC peering setups; a couple notes: ensure MTU and egress rules allow persistent GRPC streams, and if you're using customer-managed KMS, coordinate key access between your cloud and Redwood control plane if Private mode isn't used.
[20:45] Tom: if we go Private deployment, is the control plane still Redwood-managed?
[21:00] Maya: with Private you get a customer-control-plane option; you can run control plane components behind your firewall and Redwood provides the orchestration artifacts. we can discuss on the next security call.
[22:20] Carlos: back to benchmarks — i noticed some odd p95 noise on v3-small for sequences that include long embedded receipts, probably due to kv cache eviction behavior. we should test with your top-10 longest sequences.
[23:10] Lina: i'll gather sample logs and prompts for that, and we can run a focused test.
[24:05] Carlos: also quantization profile matters; v2-quant shows lower cost but sometimes fails on structured outputs — prompts that assume strict JSON output can break. we can add a pre/post-processor to enforce schema.
[25:30] Jared: we have a critical route that must always return within 600ms p95, is there a guaranteed way?
[25:50] Carlos: the only true guarantee is dedicated warm replicas pinned to a low-latency model; we can provision a dedicated pool for that route with autoscale policies that keep headroom. that's part of the Dedicated offering and costs more, but it's the pattern many customers use for SLAs.
[27:00] Marcus: what's the estimated cost for that dedicated pool? rough numbers fine.
[27:15] Maya: i'll send a back-of-envelope price — depends on throughput, but expect an incremental $Xk/month for the smallest dedicated config for standby. we'll price it in the follow-up.
[28:45] Tom: operational question: if we pin a model and later want to change it, do we need a maintenance window?
[29:05] Carlos: no maintenance window per se, you can roll traffic with canaries, but for large model weight swaps you may see transient errors; we recommend low-traffic windows for big changes and a canary strategy.
[30:20] Lina: will the prompt templates need to change between v3-small and v2-quant?
[30:40] Carlos: sometimes yes, especially with quantized models that hallucinate differently. we recommend prompt calibrations stored in the Console per model so you can version prompts alongside model pins.
[31:50] Maya: OK let's capture the plan: pin /checkout to v3-small:v3.1, fallback to v2-quant:v2.4, canary v3-medium in 10% after 48 hours of eval. pre-warm fallback and schedule SRE canary next week.
[33:05] Marcus: agreed, subject to security sign-off.
[33:30] Priya: can we get the SOC2 and SAML docs before we proceed with Dedicated?
[33:45] Maya: yes i'll attach those to the CRM and email.
[34:50] Carlos: one more note on rollback: we can script automatic rollback triggers on hallucination counts and conversion drop; but you'll need to define thresholds in advance.
[36:00] Jared: we'll draft thresholds, probably hallucination rate > 2% or conversion delta <-1.5%.
[36:30] Lina: timeline: we want initial pin in production test by 2027-01-25 and canary by 2027-01-27.
[37:00] Maya: that timeline seems tight but doable if evals finish. i'll coordinate with Carlos and SRE.
[38:10] Carlos: action items — i'll update the benchmark sheet with the 8k context runs and quant notes tonight. also will add recommended autoscale settings.
[39:20] Marcus: thanks. can you include a sample fallback trace so our SREs can simulate the route?
[39:40] Carlos: yes we'll provide a trace and a small script to simulate saturation.
[40:30] Priya: last security Q: do you support attestation for on-prem/hsm keys?
[40:45] Maya: yes for Private we support HSM and attestations; details in the security pack.
[41:55] Tom: want to confirm next meeting cadence remains weekly.
[42:05] Maya: weekly is fine, we'll keep it as a checkpoint until POC closes.
[43:10] Maya: okay final recap and owners: Carlos updates benchmarks, Lina runs evals, Maya sends security + pricing, schedule canary with Tom next week. any objections?
[43:45] Marcus: all good.
[44:00] Maya: great, i'll follow up with an email with attachments and the sheet. thanks everyone.
[44:12] (call ends)
questions: What are recovery time expectations for rollback?
Can the fallback be pre-warmed to avoid cold starts?
What metrics will trigger automatic rollback?
